chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Inform me — is recognition of the Imam from you obligatory upon all creation?' He said: 'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to all people as a Messenger and as a proof of God upon all His creatures in His earth. So whoever believes in God and in Muhammad as the Messenger of God, and follows him and ratifies him, then recognition of the Imam from us is obligatory upon him. And whoever did not believe in God and His Messenger, did not follow him, did not ratify him, and did not recognise both their rights, how can the recognition of the Imam be obligatory upon him, while he does not believe in God and His Messenger and recognise both their rights?'

He said: I said, 'So what do you say regarding one who believes in God and His Messenger and ratifies His Messenger in all that God revealed — is the right of your recognition obligatory upon them?' He said: 'Yes. Are they not recognising so-and-so and so-and-so?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you think that God is the One Who placed the recognition of those ones into their hearts? By God! It was none other than Satan who placed that into their hearts. No, by God! None but God — Mighty and Majestic — inspires the believers with our right.'

key_terms.حُجَّة: Hujja — Proof, divine authority, the established proof of God upon creation
key_terms.فُلَان: Fulan — 'So-and-so', a deliberately vague reference to unnamed rivals whose identity was understood by the original audience
key_terms.مَعْرِفَة: Ma'rifa — Recognition, knowledge of the Imam's true identity and authority, going beyond mere acquaintance to deep spiritual acknowledgement
key_terms.وَاجِبَة: Wajiba — Obligatory, a religious duty that is binding

ai.seo_question: Is recognition of the Imam obligatory in Shia Islam, and what did Imam al-Baqir say about false recognition?
ai.summary: In this theological dialogue, Zurara asks Imam al-Baqir (AS) whether recognizing the Imam is obligatory for all creation. The Imam clarifies that this obligation is conditional: it applies only to those who already believe in God and His Prophet. Crucially, the Imam exposes those who nominally claim faith yet follow false leaders (referred to cryptically as 'so-and-so and so-and-so', understood by the original audience to mean the Umayyad or non-Alid caliphs), declaring by solemn oath that such recognition was planted by Satan, while true recognition of the Imams' authority is inspired by God alone.

en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Zurara who has said the following.

“I said to abu Ja’far (a.s.), ‘Is knowing the Imam from among you obligatory on all creatures?’” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, sent Muhammad to all people as His Messenger and as His authority over all creatures on earth. Those who have faith in Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger and have followed him and have acknowledged his message on such people it is obligatory to the Imam from us. Those who do not have faith in Allah and in His messenger and who do not follow him and do not acknowledge him and do not acknowledge the rights of Allah and His messenger then knowing the Imam (a.s.) would be obligatory on them? They do not have faith in Allah and in His messenger, do not follow him and do not acknowledge their rights.”

I then asked, “What would you say about those who have faith in Allah and His messenger who acknowledge His messenger in all the matters that have come from Allah, is it obligatory for them to know the Imam (a.s.) from you?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Yes, it is obligatory. Do they not know so and so?” I said, “yes, they do.” The Imam (a.s.) then said, “Do you think Allah is the one who has placed such knowledge in their hearts? No, I swear to Allah that no one other than Satan has placed such knowledge in their hearts. I swear to Allah that no one other than Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has inspired our rights in hearts of the believers.”
